verdict_Q: NOT FOUND IN PRINT as stated (provisional). No source found that bounds the non-coverage of the Student/finite-population t interval by the quadratic majorant 1[miss] <= (1+a1 A^2+a2 Q)^2 with exact SRSWOR moments, uniform over a max|x-mean|/SD class. But the ingredients are classical, so the contribution is the combination, not the method: (i) the Chebyshev-Markov quadratic-majorant/moment-duality method (Krein-Nudelman, Karlin-Studden) is explicit in Pinelis arXiv:1011.6065 'Between Chebyshev and Cantelli' (read in full), which says it was developed for bounding P(quadratic polynomial in X >= 0) in self-normalized sums, and is used in Pinelis arXiv:1101.3286 (Berry-Esseen for Student) - but for independent summands and a Berry-Esseen goal, not SRSWOR or a t-interval class bound; (ii) Eaton 1974 / Pinelis 1994 / Dufour-Hallin 1993 give certified conservative critical values under symmetry/Rademacher (orthant-symmetric) models, with 'a traditional Chebyshev bound' min-ed with Eaton - different model (sign-flip conditional on |x|, Q constant), no population-mean-centred SRSWOR; (iii) Bloznelis-Gotze 1999 give a uniform finite-population Studentized Berry-Esseen bound but with a non-explicit absolute constant (abstract only); (iv) Bardenet-Maillard 2015 give certified empirical-Bernstein-Serfling intervals under SRSWOR but for bounded range, not t. Saw-Yang-Mo/Troffaes-Basu is Chebyshev/Cantelli with sample mean/SD but for predicting X_{n+1}. Caveat: Eaton 1974, Dufour-Hallin 1993, Pinelis 1994, Edelman 1990, Efron 1969, Eaton-Efron 1970, Basu-DasGupta 1995, Bloznelis-Gotze 1999 could NOT be read (closed or bot-blocked); judged from abstracts and secondary descriptions.
verdict_K: PARTLY ANTICIPATED IN SPIRIT, NOT IN THIS FORM (provisional). Finite-sample conservative critical values for t-type statistics with extremal laws are in print for other classes: Dufour-Hallin 1993 (tabulated Eaton/Eaton-Pinelis critical values, bounded independent non-identical/permutation settings; abstract only), Efron 1969/Eaton-Efron 1970 (orthant symmetry), Benjamini 1983 (t-test conservative only for t >= n-1 under stretching), Basu-DasGupta 1995 (infimum coverage over symmetric unimodal laws is attained at U[-1,1] for high nominal level, 0 for low), Hendriks-IJzerman-Boon-Klaassen 2006 (read in full: uniform least favourable, two-point Bernoulli has P(T=inf)=2^(1-n) > alpha for small n), Lenzi arXiv:2608.26421 (2026). Lehmann-Loh 1990/Romano 2004 give only asymptotic uniformity statements, Romano-Wolf 2000 (read) gives a non-t KS-based bounded-support interval. None found treats SRSWOR from a finite population with a class bounding max|x-mean|/SD and few-point extremal populations. Potscher-Preinerstorfer arXiv:2412.17470 (Gaussian-model size controllability) remains the nearest structural precedent already known to the project.
verdict_Lb: ESSENTIALLY KNOWN as a geometric fact; the specific SRSWOR 'band lemma' phrasing not found. t^2=(n-1)u/(n-u) with u=(sum y)^2/sum y^2 (Hotelling 1961 cone geometry; Efron 1969; Benjamini 1983), so large t forces the centred sample into a narrow cone around the diagonal. Jonsson (Bernoulli 2011, arXiv:1102.2072) Lemma 3.3 gives the sharp quantitative form: if |y_i-y_1|>=d|y_1| then n-u>=d^2/(2+2d+d^2), hence y_i/y_1 lies in a band (one-signed) when t is large. I re-verified both the identity and the sharp inequality numerically on 20000 random samples (min slack 1.5e-7, no violation). So Lb should be presented as a corollary/lemma with Jonsson 2011 and Hotelling/Efron/Benjamini cited, not as a new result.
